title: Neat — Hide YouTube Shorts
summary: Hide YouTube Shorts everywhere — Home, search, subscriptions, channels, sidebar — and open Shorts links as normal videos.
description:
Shorts gone. YouTube back to videos.

• Removes the Shorts shelf from Home, Subscriptions and search results.
• Hides the Shorts tab and Shorts shelves on channel pages, and Shorts in the sidebar menu and notifications.
• Opens any /shorts/ link as a normal video page, with a normal player and controls.
• Optional: hide comments, end-screen suggestions, the recommended sidebar or the whole Home feed, and turn off autoplay.
• One master switch and a keyboard shortcut (Alt+Shift+Y) to turn everything off and on.
• Allow list: keep everything visible on the channels you choose.
• Changes apply instantly — no page reload.
• Light and dark mode. Tiny, fast, and idle when the page is idle.

No account.
Nothing leaves your browser.
Open source.

How it works: Neat hides page elements with a style sheet inside your browser. Your settings never leave your device. To keep working when YouTube changes its layout, it downloads a signed list of hiding rules (a small JSON file of CSS selectors) — normally once a day, and never more than once an hour. That download carries no information about you, and the rules can only hide things: they cannot run code.

Neat is not affiliated with or endorsed by YouTube or Google.
singlePurpose: Hide YouTube Shorts and other distracting parts of YouTube that the user chooses.

permissionJustifications.storage: Saves the user's on/off choices, allow list and the latest hiding rules on this device.
permissionJustifications.alarms: Checks once a day for updated hiding rules so the extension keeps working when YouTube changes its layout.
permissionJustifications.host:https://www.youtube.com/*: Needed to hide elements on YouTube pages. The extension runs on no other site.

remoteCode: No. The extension downloads a JSON rules file containing only CSS selectors and labels; it is strictly validated and never executed.
